commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a 16 MiB combined stdout/stderr cap to `runSshSandboxCommand` and adds focused regression tests for normal, over-cap, partial-output, and post-cap data behavior.

PR surface: Source +34, Tests +149. Total +183 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection and PR proof: current main appends every SSH stdout/stderr chunk into arrays until close, and the PR body shows a real child-process negative control buffering 20 MiB on main. I did not run a live SSH OOM scenario in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(sandbox): bound SSH command output buffering at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `runSshSandboxCommand` in `src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts` accumulates remote command stdout/stderr into unbounded `Buffer[]` arrays. A runaway or misconfigured remote command that produces excessive output (e.g. `cat /dev/urandom`, an infinite loop, or log dump) can exhaust the gateway process memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change adds a 16 MiB combined stdout+stderr cap at the chokepoint (the `data` event handlers inside `runSshSandboxCommand`). When the cap is exceeded the child process is killed and the promise rejects with a descriptive error that includes the accumulated partial output. This matches the defensive bounding pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `MAX_POST_TOOL_CALL_BUFFER_BYTES` in the OpenAI transport stream).

No API surface or type change — the existing `SandboxBackendCommandResult` / `RunSshSandboxCommandParams` interfaces are unchanged. The 16 MiB cap is a hard fail-closed safety guard. Callers that already handle rejection (all call sites in `ssh-backend.ts` use `await` with try-catch or `.catch`) receive the new error naturally. Operations that legitimately need >16 MiB output should use sandbox file-system tools (read/write) instead of raw shell output buffering.

## User Impact

- **Before:** A remote SSH command producing >16 MiB of output could grow the gateway heap unboundedly until OOM kills the process.
- **After:** Output is capped at 16 MiB. Exceeding that limit terminates the child process and surfaces a clear `Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit` error, preserving the partial output collected up to the cap.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed
Verify that `runSshSandboxCommand` kills the child process and rejects with a byte-limit error when combined stdout+stderr exceeds 16 MiB.

### Real environment tested
- OS: Linux x64
- Node.js: v24
- Method: independent `.mts` proof script driving the real `runSshSandboxCommand` production function with a real child process (no mocked `spawn`)

### Evidence after fix (real child process, 20 MiB output)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== FIX APPLIED (real child process, 20 MiB output) ===

error: Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit
stdout buffered before kill: 15.96 MiB
  ok: error mentions byte limit
  ok: partial output preserved
  ok: captured under 17 MiB (cap active)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

Core behaviors confirmed:
| Assertion | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Error message contains "exceeded ... byte limit" | ok |
| Partial stdout preserved in error object | ok (15.96 MiB) |
| Captured output is under 17 MiB (cap is active, not leaking) | ok |

### Negative control (pre-fix main code, same script)

```
$ git show origin/main:src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts > src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== NEGATIVE CONTROL (pre-fix main code) ===

exit code: 0
stdout buffered: 20.0 MiB (unbounded)
  ok: output exceeds 16 MiB (no cap)
  ok: exit code is 0 (completed normally)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 2 passed, 0 failed
```

Before the fix, the same 20 MiB child process completes normally and ALL 20 MiB is buffered in-memory. The cap is absent — any command can exhaust heap arbitrarily.

### Vitest regression coverage

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.output-bound.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

## Evidence

- **Real behavior proof:** 3/3 assertions passed (fix), 2/2 assertions passed (negative control) — full terminal output above
- **Vitest:** 5/5 new tests pass (output-bound scenarios), 28/28 existing tests pass (no regression)
- **Lint:** clean
- **Type check:** clean

AI-assisted.
